### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4262cc52bf748a91411f08e36656044c2a6f8f0c` — the merge of head `58b68fe15e0a842e178d1b59da540f60e1a466c3` into base `69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4262cc52bf748a91411f08e36656044c2a6f8f0c && git checkout 4262cc52bf748a91411f08e36656044c2a6f8f0c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630 58b68fe15e0a842e178d1b59da540f60e1a466c3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630 && git merge --no-ff 58b68fe15e0a842e178d1b59da540f60e1a466c3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69d421805896d8d598bd27a0d035e494f7de6630` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58b68fe15e0a842e178d1b59da540f60e1a466c3`
Local-runs: none

Written 2026-10-11T17:49Z, inside the adopting seat's session. Inputs: card #22817 (body and all five comments: retriage `6110035816`, triage first touch `6110327411` = direction A, claim `6110532290`, `os-dev-report` `6111555023`, the seat's ACCEPT `6111585171` read as a claim to verify), PR #22872 (body, 5-file list, net diff against merge-base `55382dc02a`), and the 38 check-runs on the head: 34 success, 4 skipped (opt-in / path-filtered), 0 failure — Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check legs, Test Core x7, Check Changeset x2, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood x5, Temporal Conformance, the single-writer and claim checks all green. No governed path in the file list; head repo equals base repo; draft; `mergeable_state: clean`. Nothing built, run or re-run locally; every tree fact below is a `git show` / `git grep` on `refs/review/pr-22872`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The activation door accepts an action no package ships — RIGHT.** `shippingPackageOf` returns `undefined` for an environment-authored action and the row is sent without a `packageId` key, so `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.setActive` writes `package_id: null` (its existing `?? null`). The docblock at `actions.ts:146` declared exactly this; triage `6110327411` directed it (option A); ADR-0126 §4 says absence of a row means active and the ledger imposes no gate, §5's write authority (`manage_metadata`; platform operator under `group`/`isolated`) is untouched by the diff, and §8 item 2 lists what the action leg inherits from the flow leg (ledger, write authority, consult point, surface row) and names no provenance gate. The nullable `package_id` was already landed and reviewed for the security catalog (#22811 / #22621 → A; the platform-objects field description reads "Empty when no package ships it"). Not an ADR reversal under Prime Directive #13: no accepted ADR says an unpackaged action must be refused; the flow toggle's refusal is #20726's own, tied to `status`. The response body (`{ name, objectName, enabled }`) and the other refusals (404, 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 501) are unchanged. Pinned through the REAL `HttpDispatcher`, objectql projection and `ObjectStoreActionActivationStore` in the new test (object-less 200 + exact row; ON-first row; then 409 `ACTION_DISABLED` with zero executions).

2. **The package credit — RIGHT, and the deviation is inside A.** Old: `String(action._packageId ?? obj._packageId ?? '')`, which credited a standalone environment action to its route object's package, wrote the literal `'sys_metadata'` rehydration sentinel as a package, and credited a tenant-authored `_packageId: 'app.crm'` binding to that package. New: the ADR-0029 D9.6 predicate `isCodeArtifactBody` (truthy `_packageId`, not the sentinel, not `_provenance: 'org'`) on the action, else on the object only when the action is the object's own `actions[]` entry by reference. Reference identity holds: `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` (`action-execution.ts:2705`) returns `obj.actions.find(...)` itself for an embedded action, so the 73 unstamped platform actions keep their object's package (CONTROL pins: stamped `crm` and embedded-unstamped `crm`). `package_id` means "the package that ships the artifact" (ADR-0126 §4, the field's description), so the old credit made the column lie. **Readers of `sys_metadata_activation.package_id`, measured at the head — none decides anything from it:** `ActionActivationProjection.hydrate` reads `name` and `active` only; the security catalog's `readDisabledCatalogNames` (`resolve-authz-context.ts`) reads `metadata_type`, `name`, `active`; `catalog-set-in-effect.ts` and `last-admin-guard.ts` have no `package_id` read; the flow engine's hydrate reads `name`/`active`; uninstall (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`) runs domain-registered cleanups and its own comment says its `packageId` is the manifest id, never the ledger's — no uninstall path reads or deletes ledger rows by package; `highlightFields` on the platform object is display only. The changeset's "No reader decides anything from `package_id`" is therefore verified, not taken from the report.

3. **The catch → `deps.errorFromThrown(err, 503)` — RIGHT; the pairs that move, read off `resolveThrownHttpError` (`packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`):** (a) a `ValidationError` / `{ code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', fields }` with no status: was `503 VALIDATION_FAILED`, now `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `details.fields` (pinned); (b) a throw spelling `.statusCode` only: was the 503 fallback, now its declared status (#7525's rule); (c) an unregistered `.code` string (a driver errno) on an undeclared 5xx: was served verbatim in the closed `error.code` slot, now the status-derived `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with the spelling withheld (#12509) — the old catch violated ADR-0112's closed vocabulary here; (d) `issues`/`userMessage` now ride through. Unchanged: the engine's own `{ status: 503, code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' }` (no ledger attached) keeps its pair; a bare `Error` is `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (pinned) and still passes the 5xx leak withhold, since both the old and the new path end in `this.error`. A registered `.code` with no status still lands at the 503 fallback with that code — the shared resolver's own rule, identical to before, so nothing moves and the door now has no rule of its own, which is what the card asked for. Same exit the catalog door adopted in #22811.

4. **`InMemoryMetadataActivationStore.setActive` refusing `''` — RIGHT; no consumer relied on the leniency.** One `refuseEmptyPackageId` called by both stores (Route & surface ownership rule 1: one owner), the durable store's message byte-identical. Consumers at the head: objectql's `InMemoryActionActivationStore` (used only in `action-activation.test.ts`, every write `packageId: 'crm'`); service-automation's `InMemoryFlowActivationStore` (six test files, none passing `''`; the one non-test write, `toggleFlow` → `flowActivationStore.setActive({ packageId: packageOwner })`, follows a 409 refusal for any flow no package ships, and `packagedFlowOwner` returns a package id or `undefined`, never `''`). The repo-wide grep for `packageId: ''` on an activation store hits only the core refusal pins. The `MetadataActivationRow.packageId` contract already declared `''` refused; the double was the one out of contract.

5. **The new `@objectstack/metadata-core` import in `packages/runtime` — RIGHT.** `@objectstack/metadata-core: workspace:*` is already in `packages/runtime/package.json` `dependencies` (the PR does not touch that file); `isCodeArtifactBody` and `isTenantAuthored` are exported through `export * from './code-artifact-provenance.js'` in its index; `check:undeclared-dep-imports` and the four Type Check legs are green on the head. Asking the one D9.6 predicate instead of a bare `_packageId` read is the right owner.

6. **The docblock correction — RIGHT.** "Neither does the flow toggle" has been false since `c8111a575` (2026-09-30, #20726): `automation.ts:2202` documents and the door enforces 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` for a flow no package ships, naming the flow's own `status` switch. `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` records `visible` and `disabled` as objectui-only CEL rendering predicates, and a grep of `action-execution.ts`, `domains/actions.ts`, objectql `engine.ts` and `action-activation.ts` finds no dispatch-side read of either. So the stated reason (an action has no server-side switch of its own) is measured, and the corrected sentence narrows the claim to what is enforced (Prime Directive #10).

7. **Stale sibling wording the widening leaves behind — noted, not a defect.** Outside the claim's file surface and not touched: the `sys-metadata-activation.object.ts` header still says "flows and actions reach this ledger only when a package ships them"; objectql's `action-activation.ts` header still says "for PACKAGED ACTIONS"; and `describeDisabled`'s served 409 sentence says "Re-enable the packaged action" — now also served for an environment-authored one (the remedy stays right). Code comments and one refusal sentence, no published page; `metadata-lifecycle.mdx:140` stays true. Carried as a note for the seat (see ③).

8. **Public surface, net:** `@objectstack/runtime` — the door's accept-set widens (unpackaged actions), one status pair corrects (503 → 400 on validation), the row credit narrows to the shipping package; response shape unchanged; no new route, no query parameter read, nothing for `/discovery`. `@objectstack/core` — `InMemoryMetadataActivationStore.setActive` throws `TypeError` on `''`. No `packages/objectql`, no `packages/spec`, no docs, no governed path. The pinned objectui sibling imports nothing removed or renamed.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22817-action-activation-unpackaged.md`: `@objectstack/runtime: minor`, `@objectstack/core: minor` — matches what the diff publishes. The runtime change is a widening of a REST door, so at least minor; the core change brings the double into the contract the row already declared (`''` refused), so it is a fix rather than a narrowing of the declared contract, and the shared minor covers it; `(narrowing)` would be wrong. Each bullet carries FROM → TO and the one-line fix ("omit the key"), names both subclasses, and the ADR-0112 bullet states the exact pairs. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as non-breaking, so no disposition marker is owed. PR body line 2 is the bare `Clause-②: yes`, the changeset `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — both legal spellings of the same declaration. Both Check Changeset runs on the head are green.

Clause-②: yes (widening)

### ③ Boundary flags

The report has `open_questions: []`; its eight `deviations` and one `out_of_scope_findings` entry are the flags.

- **Scope within A (no credit to the route object's package):** answered RIGHT in ①2; triage's own wording ("passes `undefined` for an action no package ships") covers it; the changeset states it as its own bullet; the measured census (144/146 unchanged) is consistent with the CONTROL pins.
- **Route (c) pinned as 400 + undeclared 503; declared-pair 503 kept by the existing posture-gate case:** answered, consistent with ①3.
- **"Back on, the row is UPDATED" not pinned at the door; update double dropped so `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` is untouched:** acceptable. The door's ON-first row is pinned; the package-less update leg is pinned in core ("UPDATES its row with no package on the way back on"); the OFF-then-ON sequence through the store is pinned in objectql's `action-activation.test.ts`. Not writing the pinned ledger from a feature PR is the right call.
- **Throwaway dogfood case deleted, never committed:** the file list confirms five files; answered.
- **Commit trailers:** both pushed non-merge commits carry `Co-authored-by: Claude` and `Claude-Session`, the AGENTS.md pair; answered.
- **Branch 3 commits behind `main`, none touching the five files:** CI runs the merge ref and it is green; `mergeable_state: clean`; answered.
- **Bare `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body vs the arm in the changeset:** answered in ②.
- **No docs edit:** verified against `metadata-lifecycle.mdx:140`; answered. The stale sibling comments in ①7 are outside the claim's surface (`packages/objectql` was forbidden to this PR) and are a comment-and-sentence drift, not a defect — the seat should carry them as an acceptance note or a small follow-up on the engine lane, ⛔ not as a change to this PR.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`check-objectql-double-limit` lifts identifiers from comments, tripped TDZ, answered UNJUDGED):** the gate failed loud, so no verdict on this PR rests on it, and the PR is green after a comment reword. Escalated, not blocking: it is reproducible with a named landing point (`identifiersIn` in `scripts/check-objectql-double-limit.mjs`), which is Prime Directive #10's filing shape; the seat's "noted, not filed" should become a tooling card the next time it costs a round, or now if the seat prefers.
- **The card's stop clause** ("a real product reason that an environment-authored action must not have an install-level switch"): the report's measurement supports going ahead. Actions carry no server-side switch (`visible`/`disabled` are objectui-only — ①6), so the flow toggle's reason (#20726: the flow's own `status`) does not transfer; ADR-0126 §8 item 2 names no provenance gate; the security catalog already switches environment-authored items (#22811). One property to state rather than hide, pre-existing and unchanged by this PR: the row identity is `(metadata_type, name)` deployment-wide (ADR-0126 §4, ADR-0131 D6), so an operator switching off an environment action by name in a `group`/`isolated` posture switches off every same-named action; `refuseAmbiguousActionActivation` sees the declarations the current kernel's metadata service enumerates. Environment actions on packaged objects already landed rows before this PR, so nothing newly reachable opens; the §5 operator gate holds. Not a product reason against A.
- **Who may call the door:** unchanged by the diff (steps 1-4 untouched); the widening opens no new caller.
